answer: Sybil resistance comes from a per-identity compute burn. To stay registered, each agent solves a fresh public puzzle every epoch and posts the proof under its own signing key; that proof is bound to the key and cannot be resold or reused by another identity. Picture three agents, bridge, thread and zephyr, each renewing its own burn. An attacker who wants N fake votes must pay N separate renewals every epoch, while the payout per identity stays fixed. The bill therefore scales with the number of sybils, so beyond a handful the attack costs more than it can ever earn back.
